choices.choice: converged; very considerable; language stocks; development
choices.reason: Convergence does not assert mixing; absolute/elative superlative does not require a formal ranking. The grammar makes the stocks and attained Bildung linguistic. No modern genealogical rank or universal Bildung equivalent is asserted.

choices.choice: national distinctiveness; distinctive traits; immigration (mass noun)
choices.reason: Related distinctive vocabulary preserves the conceptual connection; retain national without equating it with a nation-state. Mass immigration covers the plural events and supplies the repeated elliptical noun.

choices.reason: Remove added activity noun and causative passive. Keep the peoples as the subject entering the state. Different English phrasing expresses the repeated self-relation without imposing one awkward formula.

choices.term: solange ... kennen; bis auf ... Unterjochung; frei von fremdem Einfluss
choices.choice: known historical interval; down to subjugation by Europeans; freedom as an adjunct
choices.reason: Temporal reading of bis auf is retained alongside the knowledge limit. The exceptive reading remains possible. Keep the freedom phrase within the entry-into-ferment clause; the second predicate follows in a new English sentence without adding a new temporal bridge.

choices.choice: wearing-down; self-contained native interaction; anything foreign
choices.reason: Retain abrasion rather than making equalisation the asserted outcome. Interaction differs from contact in s5; native contrasts with foreign. The reflexive stays with the interaction, not an inserted continent noun. Self-contained is understood here at the passage’s collective level, not as isolation of each community. Anything foreign avoids narrowing to discrete linguistic elements.
